title: Behold the Blind Their Sight Receive
description: Behold the Blind Their Sight Receive in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 137, headed “Miracles in the life, death, and resurrection of Christ”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold the blind their sight re-ceive; Be-hold the dead a-wake and live; The dumb speak won-ders, and the lame Leap like the hart, and bless his Name.

lines: Behold the blind their sight receive;
Behold the dead awake and live;
The dumb speak wonders, and the lame
Leap like the hart, and bless his Name.
Thus doth th' eternal Spirit own
And seal the mission of the Son;
While he hangs bleeding on the cross.
He dies; the heavens in mourning stood;
He rises, and appears a God;
No more to bleed, no more to die.
Hence and for ever from my heart
I bid my doubts and fears depart;
And to those hands my soul resign

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
